name: python-lint-undefined-name-asks
desc: `helper` is enrolled as a REPO-WIDE known symbol (defined in a different file), so the additive hallucination check resolves it and stays silent — isolating this ask to lint alone, the same way callshape.json's fixtures isolate call-shape from the additive check. Ruff, unlike the additive check, has no cross-file knowledge: it sees `helper` used with no local def/import and flags F821. Proves the ask reports a true file line number (2), not the hunk-relative 'snippet line N' every other hook-mode check carries.

name: python-lint-syntax-error-clean
desc: ruff emits `invalid-syntax` diagnostics UNCONDITIONALLY — `--select F821,F811` does not suppress them (verified against 0.16.1). Without the explicit rule filter in lintFindingsWithReason this Write asks with a header claiming '(F821/F811)' over a parser error, and lintSymbolFromMessage puts punctuation (')' out of "Expected `)`, found newline") into decisionRecord.Symbols — the field guardstats buckets per-symbol and fpaudit dedups on. A file the interpreter cannot parse is also not a resolution question: it fails loudly at runtime with or without the guard.

name: python-lint-additive-overlap-adds-nothing
desc: The firewall against the additive check. `totally_made_up` resolves nowhere, so the ALWAYS-ON additive check flags it — and ruff independently flags the same name F821, since 'undefined name' and 'not found in the indexed code' are the same question asked twice. ask_without_flag is the shape built for exactly this (the file-scope firewall): it asserts flag-OFF already asks, then that flag-ON produces a BYTE-IDENTICAL reason. A plain expect_ask fixture cannot see this defect — removing the firewall only DOUBLES an existing ask, which an ask/no-ask assertion reads as unchanged.

name: python-lint-edit-tool-clean
desc: Lint is Write-only in v1. The hunk is deliberately a COMPLETE, VALID standalone Python snippet carrying a real F811 (`fetch` redefined at hunk line 4) — NOT a fragment. That matters for what this fixture can detect: an earlier cut used a fragment, which relied on ruff's invalid-syntax diagnostic to produce the ask when the tool-gate was removed, and the moment lintFindingsWithReason started filtering non-selected rules (correctly) that fixture went silent for BOTH the intact and the mutated gate — proving nothing while still passing. With a genuine F811 in the hunk, removing the tool-gate makes lint run on Edit text and ask, so this fixture actually kills lint/tool-gate. Flag-off stays silent because `fetch` is defined in the hunk itself, so the additive check resolves it.

name: python-lint-non-python-clean
desc: Lint only runs on Python. The content is deliberately VALID PYTHON carrying a real F811, placed in a .go file — so the only thing keeping this fixture silent is the language gate, not ruff failing to find anything. (The previous cut put valid Go here, which ruff can only report as invalid-syntax; once that rule is correctly filtered out, removing the lang-gate produced no ask and the fixture stopped detecting the mutation.) `fetch` is enrolled so the always-on additive check — which reads Python `def` lines in a .go file as an unresolved reference — resolves it and stays quiet; there are no qualified `pkg.Sel()` call sites for the same-repo/deps-go checks either.

name: python-lint-isolated-config-still-asks
desc: Proves --isolated is actually applied. Uses `[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]` rather than a plain `ignore = [...]`: measured directly against this repo's installed ruff (0.16.1), an explicit CLI `--select F821,F811` already overrides a config's top-level `ignore` regardless of --isolated, which would make a plain-ignore fixture pass for the wrong reason (vacuously, since neither flags/no-flags nor isolated/not-isolated would move it). per-file-ignores is the mechanism CLI --select does NOT override — confirmed empirically: without --isolated this same config silences the F821 finding below; with --isolated (what lint.go always passes) it does not, so the ask still fires.
